original_question: Solved problem record: if V is a variety of residually ordered l-groups and satisfies no group laws, must V contain a free linearly ordered group, and is V = R?
target_in_paper: Section 1.2, solved Problem 1.11: the item asking whether a variety V of residually ordered ℓ-groups with no nontrivial group laws must contain a free linearly ordered group and whether such a V must actually coincide with R = RO, the variety of all residually ordered ℓ-groups. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s own formulation. It correctly identifies the ambient object V as a variety of residually ordered ℓ-groups, keeps the hypothesis about absence of group laws, and preserves both conclusions the paper asks about: containment of a free linearly ordered group and equality V = R. It also correctly recognizes that this appears in the paper as a solved-problem record rather than as an open problem. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))
missing_details: The paper’s ambient category is ℓ-groups, i.e. lattice-ordered groups; expanding that notation makes the question stand-alone. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))

A residually ordered ℓ-group is defined in the paper as a subdirect product of ordered groups; the paper also notes the synonymous terms o-approximable and representable. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))
R is not generic notation: the paper explicitly defines R = RO to be the variety of all residually ordered ℓ-groups. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))

To be fully explicit, “satisfies no group laws” should be read as meaning that the underlying groups in V satisfy no nontrivial group identity. This is implicit in the problem statement and is not unpacked in the paper. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))

For a stand-alone formulation, “free linearly ordered group” can be glossed as a free totally ordered group, since the paper uses the ordered/linearly ordered terminology without further local definition. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))
refined_question: Let V be a variety of residually ordered ℓ-groups, meaning lattice-ordered groups that are subdirect products of ordered groups. Assume that the underlying groups of members of V satisfy no nontrivial group law. Must V contain a free linearly ordered (totally ordered) group, and must V in fact be exactly R = RO, the variety of all residually ordered ℓ-groups? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))
justification: This is the nearest official formulation in the paper: your draft matches Section 1.2, Problem 1.11 essentially verbatim. The only paper-faithful refinements needed are to expand ℓ-group, spell out the paper’s definition of “residually ordered,” and identify R as the notation for the full variety of residually ordered ℓ-groups. The paper also records that the answer is Yes and attributes the solution reference to Medvedev [69], so the target is specifically a solved-problem entry. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))
